focus: 'have to' /hæftə/ · 'has to' /hæstə/ · 'should' /ʃʊd/ (silent l) · 'must' /mʌst/ · weak 'to' in obligation · 'ought to' /ɔːtə/
focus_ar: 'have to' /hæftə/، و 'has to' /hæstə/، و 'should' (l صامتة)، و 'must'، و 'to' الخفيفة، و 'ought to'
arabic_challenge: 'Have to' is pronounced /hæftə/ (with an /f/!) and 'has to' as /hæstə/ (with /s/) — the voiced /v/ and /z/ assimilate to voiceless before 'to'. Learners who say 'hav-to' sound unnatural. 'Should' has a silent 'l' that is often wrongly pronounced.

isolation.instructions: 'Have to' (obligation) is pronounced /hæftə/ — the /v/ becomes an /f/ before the voiceless 't', and 'to' weakens to /tə/. Say 'haff-tuh', not 'have-too'.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'have to' (إلزام) تُنطق /hæftə/ — الـ /v/ بتبقى /f/ قبل 't'، و 'to' بتخف. قول 'هافـتـه' مش 'هاف-تو'.
practice: I have to go = I haff-tə go

sentence_practice: I have to go to work early.
daily_drills.record_this: I have to go to work early tomorrow. We have to wait here for the bus, and they have to finish the project today.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'have to go'. Does it sound like 'haff-tə go', with an /f/?

isolation.instructions: 'Has to' becomes /hæstə/ — the /z/ of 'has' turns to /s/ before the voiceless 't'. Say 'hass-tuh'. Same assimilation as 'have to → hafta'.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'has to' تبقى /hæstə/ — الـ /z/ في 'has' تتحول لـ /s/ قبل 't'. قول 'هاسـتـه'.

sentence_practice: She has to work on Saturday.
He has to wake up early.
The student has to finish the test.
daily_drills.record_this: She has to work on Saturday this week. He has to wake up early for his new job, and every student has to finish the test on time.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'she has to go'. Is it 'she hass-tə go', with an /s/?

isolation.instructions: 'Should' is /ʃʊd/ — the 'l' is SILENT, and the vowel is the short /ʊ/ (like 'book'). Same for 'would' /wʊd/ and 'could' /kʊd/. Say 'shood', not 'shoo-ld'.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'should' تُنطق /ʃʊd/ — الـ 'l' صامتة والحرف /ʊ/ قصير (زي book). زيها 'would' و 'could'.

daily_drills.record_this: You should see a doctor about that cough. We should leave now before the traffic. And you really shouldn't eat so late at night.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'should'. Is the 'l' completely silent, with a short /ʊ/ vowel?

isolation.instructions: 'Must' is /mʌst/ with the short central /ʌ/. In 'mustn't' the FIRST 't' is silent: /ˈmʌsnt/. 'Must' is strong obligation, so it can carry more stress than 'have to'.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'must' /mʌst/ بحرف /ʌ/ قصير. في 'mustn't' الـ 't' الأولى صامتة: /ˈmʌsnt/. 'must' إلزام قوي.

daily_drills.record_this: You must wear a seatbelt in the car. You mustn't smoke here — it's not allowed. We must be careful, but you don't have to worry too much.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'mustn't'. Is the first 't' silent, so it sounds like 'muss-nt'?

isolation.instructions: 'Ought to' reduces to /ɔːtə/ ('or-tuh'). Across all these modals, 'to' stays weak (/tə/): have to, ought to, going to. Advice flows smoothly: 'you-ought-tə-rest'.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'ought to' بتتقلّص لـ /ɔːtə/. وفي كل دول 'to' بتفضل خفيفة: have to، ought to. النصيحة بتسيل بسلاسة.

sentence_practice: We ought to call the doctor.
daily_drills.record_this: You ought to rest more and you ought to drink more water. We ought to call the doctor tomorrow. Honestly, you ought to try a little harder.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'ought to rest'. Does 'to' stay weak (/tə/), flowing into 'rest'?

challenge_sentences: I have to work, but you should rest.
She has to leave early and she mustn't be late.
We ought to call the doctor.
You must wear a seatbelt but you don't have to hurry.
daily_drills.record_this: I have to work today, but you should rest at home. She has to leave early and she mustn't be late. We ought to call the doctor about your cough. You must wear a seatbelt in the car, but you don't have to hurry.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: 'have to' = hafta, 'has to' = hasta, and 'should' with a silent l.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself giving rules and advice. Then listen back and check each feature.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك وانت تدّي قواعد ونصائح، وبعدين اسمع وراجع كل نقطة.
test_yourself.passage: Let me tell you about the rules at my new job. I have to arrive at eight every morning, and I have to wear a uniform. My manager has to check everyone in. We mustn't use our phones during work, and we mustn't be late. But we don't have to work on Fridays, which is nice. If you feel sick, you should tell your manager and you ought to rest at home. You must follow the safety rules, and you should always ask if you're not sure. I think everyone has to start somewhere, so you shouldn't worry too much on your first day.

sounds_to_check.'have to' /hæftə/: I have to arrive, I have to wear, we don't have to work
sounds_to_check.'has to' /hæstə/: my manager has to check, everyone has to start
sounds_to_check.'should' /ʃʊd/ (silent l): you should tell, you should always ask, you shouldn't worry
sounds_to_check.'must/mustn't': you must follow, we mustn't use, we mustn't be late

scoring_guide.90_100: 'hafta/hasta' assimilation is natural and 'should' has a silent l. A2 obligation phrasing is solid — ready for week 12.
scoring_guide.50_69: 'have to' pronounced 'have-too', or 'l' sounded in 'should'. Repeat days 1-3.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5, saying each modal + weak 'to' as one chunk.

for_arabic_speakers: 'have to' → /hæftə/ (with /f/), 'has to' → /hæstə/ (with /s/). This assimilation is normal, natural English.
'should', 'would', 'could' have a SILENT 'l' and a short /ʊ/ vowel.
'to' stays weak (/tə/) after all these modals — never a strong 'two'.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
